motivation: Quantify explicit opponent-designed-rush early success -> multi-series sustained drives -> scoring PPD and shared 60-minute clock opportunities, residual to Build16. Avoid re-adding raw rush EPA.

training.model: One coefficient ridge fit to pregame drive-chain excess versus Build16 signed margin residual, lambda=25

reasons: No pooled or severe cohort paired-bootstrap 95% interval excluding zero
Pooled mean error reduction ~0.045 points per game, smaller than prespecified 0.15-point requirement
Fitted negative sign inconsistent with the intuitive causality that new sustained drives automatically add scoring beyond already modeled rush/third-down EPA
No prospectively archived ATS outcome for this new mechanism, regardless of authentic free odds now being captured
promotion.research_mode: optional possession_response argument in same Build16 mechanism; never passed from standard pregame production

data_provenance.source: free historical ESPN/SportsDataverse college-football PBP; source captured retrospectively
data_provenance.clock: Verified real regulation play/drive elapsed from strict clock audit, no time proxy
data_provenance.runs: same random seed and actual 5000 outcomes per compared matchup

conclusion: Real possession-scoring/clock interaction is built, reproducibly tested and rejected for default promotion; primary predictions may still underweight a specific rushing matchup. Maintain mandatory matchup stress and collect forward evidence. Never claim the failure fixed.
